data.name: Insane
data.detailed_description:
!nsane is a nod to the cult game "Logical" from the good old Amiga days. It's all about balls and twist locks. You have to arrange the balls in the right order to pick the lock. What sounds simple enough quickly turns out to be a uniquely tricky game.

Collect four balls of the same color in a twist lock and blow them up. To beat a level, you have to pick each lock at least once. Every level adds new elements like traffic lights, one-way streets and color changers, and you also have to keep an eye out for the indestructible black balls!

!nsane features 50 exciting levels that really get your brains working. The difficultly increases progressively. Its initial levels are easy, but !nsane rapidly becomes an absorbing and addictively intricate puzzle!

Features

  • Cult game remake
  • Classic "Logical" rules
  • 50 challenging levels
  • Loads of game elements like traffic lights, one-way streets and color changers
  • Progressive difficulty

reviews.review:
Developed by VIS-Games and published by United Independent Entertainment, Insane delivers a puzzle experience that embraces simplicity while steadily building toward genuinely demanding challenges. Inspired by the classic title Logical from the Amiga era, the game modernizes a familiar concept without overcomplicating its foundation. Instead of relying on fast reflexes or elaborate storytelling, it focuses entirely on problem solving, asking players to think several moves ahead as they manipulate colored balls through interconnected mechanisms. It is a niche experience designed for fans of traditional logic games, and it remains faithful to that philosophy from beginning to end.

The gameplay revolves around arranging colored balls inside rotating twist locks until four matching balls are grouped together, allowing them to disappear while activating every lock within the level. Although the objective sounds straightforward, the difficulty increases naturally as new mechanics are introduced. One-way paths, traffic signals, color-changing elements, and immovable black balls gradually transform simple puzzles into layered brainteasers that require careful planning and experimentation. Every addition expands the strategic possibilities without abandoning the accessible core mechanics, making the learning curve feel fair while still offering meaningful complexity for experienced puzzle enthusiasts.

One of the game's strongest qualities is its level design. Each of the 50 handcrafted stages presents a distinct challenge that encourages players to analyze the entire board before making a move. Random guessing is rarely rewarded, as even a single misplaced action can force players to rethink their approach. The progression consistently introduces fresh situations that build upon previously learned mechanics, giving the campaign a satisfying sense of momentum. Completing the more advanced puzzles creates a genuine feeling of accomplishment because success comes from understanding the systems rather than memorizing solutions.

Visually, Insane adopts a clean and functional presentation that prioritizes readability over spectacle. The colorful pieces stand out clearly against the puzzle boards, making it easy to identify important elements during more complicated scenarios. Animations remain smooth and unobtrusive, while the interface stays simple enough to keep the player's attention focused on solving puzzles instead of navigating menus. The presentation may not impress players looking for modern visual flair, but it effectively serves the gameplay by ensuring every mechanic remains easy to recognize at a glance.

The game's minimalist nature is both an advantage and a limitation. Players who enjoy carefully constructed logic puzzles will appreciate the steady increase in challenge and the absence of unnecessary distractions. However, those expecting narrative progression, multiple gameplay modes, or significant variety outside the core puzzle formula may find the experience repetitive after extended play sessions. Since nearly every aspect of the game revolves around solving increasingly complex puzzles, enjoyment largely depends on how much satisfaction players find in overcoming intellectual challenges. Some of the later stages can also become quite demanding, potentially discouraging more casual players.

Insane succeeds by delivering exactly what it promises: a thoughtful puzzle game built around clever mechanics and progressively challenging level design. Its straightforward presentation and classic inspiration allow the carefully crafted puzzles to take center stage, creating an experience that rewards patience, observation, and logical thinking. While it may not appeal to everyone due to its specialized focus, fans of cerebral puzzle games will likely appreciate its refined gameplay loop and satisfying sense of progression. Developer VIS-Games and publisher United Independent Entertainment have created a title that respects the traditions of classic puzzle gaming while remaining accessible to modern audiences. 

Rating: 5/10
